name: Rat Distortion
description: The RAT. A hard, gritty distortion with a filter knob that works backwards — the sound of a lot of alternative and noise rock.

name: PI Fuzz
description: The Big Muff. Enormous sustain and a scooped midrange, which is why it disappears in a band unless the amp puts the mids back.

name: Tube Drive 3-Knob
description: The Tube Driver — a real valve inside a pedal. Warm and amp-like rather than fizzy, and famously David Gilmour's.

name: Super OD
description: The BOSS SD-1. A Tube Screamer with asymmetrical clipping — a bit brighter and less mid-humped than a TS.

name: Treble Boost
description: A sixties treble booster. Cuts the bass before the amp so a cranked valve amp stays tight instead of turning to mud.

name: T808 OD
description: The TS-808 Tube Screamer. The mid-hump is the whole point: it pushes an amp where a band leaves room, which is why it never went away.

name: Fat Rat
basedOn: modded Pro Co RAT with LED clipping
description: A RAT with LED clipping — louder, more open, and less compressed than the stock pedal.

name: T808 Mod
description: A modded TS-808 with the mid-hump reduced and more low end let through.

name: Octave Distortion
description: The Octavia. Fuzz with an octave above it, which only tracks cleanly high on the neck — that is the sound, not a fault.

name: Plus Distortion
description: The MXR Distortion+. Soft, slightly compressed, and much politer than the name suggests.

name: Full OD
description: The Fulltone Full-Drive 2 — a Tube Screamer with more range and a boost switch for when you want it louder rather than dirtier.

name: Blues OD
description: The Marshall Bluesbreaker. Low gain and very transparent, and the circuit half the modern boutique overdrives descend from.

name: Shred Distortion
description: The Marshall Shredmaster — nineties British distortion, and the sound of a lot of shoegaze.

name: M-Zone Distortion
description: The Metal Zone. Massively scooped with a powerful mid sweep, and universally either loved or loathed.

name: Bender Fuzz
description: The Tone Bender. The British fuzz of the sixties — thicker and more aggressive than a Fuzz Face.

name: BB Pre
description: The Xotic BB Preamp. A clean-ish boost with real EQ, for pushing an amp without changing what it sounds like.

name: Master Fuzz
description: The Maestro Fuzz-Tone — the first fuzz pedal, and the one on Satisfaction. Raspy and splattery by modern standards.

name: Face Fuzz
description: The Fuzz Face. Cleans up beautifully from the guitar's volume knob, which is most of why people still chase it.

name: Eternal Love
description: The Lovepedal Eternity — a Tube Screamer variant with more clarity and less midrange bump.

name: Esoteric ACB
description: The Xotic AC Booster. A low-gain overdrive that adds body without obviously colouring the amp.

name: Esoteric RCB
description: The Xotic RC Booster — a clean boost with tone controls, for making a good amp louder without changing it.

name: Zen Master
description: The Hermida Zendrive. Built to get a Dumble-style lead sound out of an ordinary amp, and it does it better than most.

name: Tube Drive 4-Knob
description: The four-knob Tube Driver, with a bias control that lets it run from smooth to spluttering.

name: SDD Preamp
description: The preamp stage from a Korg SDD-3000 delay — an eighties colouration people chase for its own sake.

name: FET Preamp
basedOn: possibly based on the BOSS FA-1 FET Amplifier
description: A clean FET preamp, for adding level and a little hardness before an amp.

name: Suhr Riot Ge (R)
description: The Suhr Riot with germanium clipping — the smoothest and most compressed of its three voices.

name: Micro Boost
description: The MXR Micro Amp. One knob, no tone controls, nothing but more — the honest clean boost.

name: Timothy Mid
description: The Timmy. Almost perfectly transparent, with bass and treble cuts that let you shape what the amp gets.

name: Blackglass 7K
description: The Darkglass B7K — a modern bass distortion with a clean blend, so the low end survives the dirt.

name: Suhr Riot LED (L)
description: The Riot with LED clipping — the loudest and most open of the three.

name: Timothy Up
description: The Timmy set brighter, letting more top end through to the amp.

name: Tone of Kings
description: The Analog Man King of Tone. Two low-gain drives in one box, and a waiting list measured in years.

name: Heartpedal 11
description: A Lovepedal amp-in-a-box — more gain and more midrange than a boost, without the fizz.

name: Jam Ray
description: The Jan Ray. A low-gain drive built around the old blackface Fender voice.

name: Suhr Riot LED/Si (M)
description: The Riot's middle voice, between the germanium smoothness and the LED openness.

name: OD 250
description: The DOD 250 reissue — a simple, raw overdrive, close cousin to the MXR Distortion+.

name: Timothy Down
description: The Timmy with the top rolled off, for taming a bright amp.

name: TS9DX +
description: The Turbo Tube Screamer in one of its hotter modes — more gain and more low end than a standard TS9.

name: Box o' Crunch
description: The MI Audio Crunch Box — a British-voiced distortion in a pedal, aimed at Marshall tones from a clean amp.

name: OD 250 Gray
description: The original grey DOD 250. A little rougher and more characterful than the reissue.

name: Horizon Precision Drive
description: Built for modern metal: a tight overdrive with a noise gate and an aggressive high-pass, for chugging in low tunings.

name: Compulsion Distortion LP
description: The Fulltone OCD in its lower-gain mode — amp-like and responsive rather than obviously a pedal.

name: Hoodoo Drive
description: A straightforward valve-voiced overdrive, aimed at pushing an amp rather than replacing it.

name: Compulsion Distortion HP
description: The OCD's high-gain mode, with considerably more saturation.

name: TS9DX Hot
description: The Turbo Tube Screamer at its most aggressive setting.

name: DS1 Distortion
description: The BOSS DS-1. Cheap, harsh, and on a great many records — Kurt Cobain and Joe Satriani both used one.

name: DS1 Distortion Mod
description: A modded DS-1, with the harshest of the top end taken out and more low end let through.

name: MCMLXXXI Drive
description: The 1981 DRV — a modern high-gain drive built around the RAT idea with far more control.

name: Sonic Drive
description: The SD-9 Sonic Distortion. More aggressive and less mid-humped than a Tube Screamer.

name: Valve Screamer VS9
description: The TS9. Brighter and a little harder than the 808, and the one most people actually owned.

name: Maxoff 808
description: The Maxon OD-808 — the same circuit as the original Tube Screamer, from the company that built them.

name: Klone Chiron
description: The Klon. Famously transparent, famously expensive, and it really does add body without swamping the amp.

name: Esoteric Bass RCB
description: The bass version of the RC Booster, with the low end left intact.

name: BB Pre AT
description: A hotter-gain version of the BB Preamp.

name: Griddle Cake
description: The Crowther Hot Cake — a thick, open overdrive that stays clear under a lot of gain.

name: Bosom Boost
description: Friedman's boost, voiced to tighten and push a high-gain amp rather than to distort on its own.

name: OD-One Overdrive
description: The BOSS OD-1, the first of the line. Simple, soft and warm — the pedal the SD-1 grew out of.

name: Sunrise Splendor Hi-Cut
description: The Morning Glory with the top end rolled back.

name: Gauss Drive
description: Mesa's own overdrive, voiced to push a Mesa without fighting the amp's midrange.

name: Sunrise Splendor
description: The JHS Morning Glory — a very transparent low-gain drive in the Bluesbreaker tradition.

name: Integral Pre
description: A clean preamp, for level and a little shaping ahead of the amp.

name: PI Fuzz - Triangle
description: The earliest Big Muff. Brighter and less scooped than the ones that followed, so it sits in a mix more easily.

name: PI Fuzz - Ram's Head
basedOn: Electro-Harmonix '70s Big Muff Pi Ram's Head
description: The seventies Big Muff — smoother and darker than the Triangle, and the one on a lot of famous records.

name: Colortone Booster
description: The Colorsound Power Boost — a loud, raw sixties boost, and part of the early Gilmour sound.

name: Colortone OD
description: The Colorsound Overdriver — the same family, with more gain and a fierce top end.

name: MOSFET Distortion
description: The Ibanez Mostortion. A mid-gain distortion with proper three-band EQ, much loved by session players.

name: PI Fuzz - Russian
description: The Russian-made Big Muff. Darker and woollier than the American ones, with a thick, heavy low end.

name: Super Fuzz
description: The Univox Super-Fuzz. Octave-flavoured, enormously thick, and completely uncompromising.

name: Tube Drive 5-Knob
basedOn: Butler Tube Driver / Dean Markley Overlord
description: The fullest Tube Driver, with the most control over how the valve is run.

name: 77 Custom OD
basedOn: MXR M77 Custom Badass Modified O.D.
description: The MXR Custom Badass — a modern mid-gain overdrive that goes further than a Tube Screamer.

name: Angry Chuck
description: The JHS Angry Charlie — a JCM800 in a box, and a good one.

name: Guardian Photon Speed
description: The Greer Lightspeed — a very clean, very transparent boost that mostly just makes things better.

name: Paradigm Shifter
description: A drive with a variable clipping character, so the same pedal can be soft or hard-edged.

name: PI Fuzz - Bass
description: A Big Muff voiced for bass, with the low end kept underneath the fuzz instead of being eaten by it.

name: Royal Bass DI
description: A valve-voiced bass preamp and DI, for going straight to the desk with a real tone.
